result.summary: RECONSTRUCTED HANDOFF -- written 2026-09-03 after the fact from the run's real, on-disk evidence: the current lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex carries an inline comment on do_attempt_dispatch/2's :catalog_service clause reading 'BLOCKER fix (TEST-DESIGNER finding, queue task 415): route_kind: :catalog_service must call catalog_lookup_stub/2, not http_transport/3' -- direct, on-disk textual confirmation this finding was real and attributed to TEST-DESIGNER. Timestamps are reconstructed approximations. TWO REAL IMPLEMENTATION DEFECTS found (not merely coverage gaps -- these are bugs in ELIXIR-DEV's shipped code, correctly reported rather than worked around, since TEST-DESIGNER's own role does not touch lib/). DEFECT 1 (BLOCKER-shaped correctness bug): route_kind: :catalog_service never actually routed to catalog_lookup_stub/2 in the pre-rework2 do_attempt_dispatch/2 -- every row, regardless of route_kind, went through http_transport/3's URL-dispatch path. Empirically verified via a scratch probe issuing a real dispatch against a synthetic :catalog_service row: it reached a genuine :httpc.request/4 call against a URL built from the row's service_id rather than being rejected before any HTTP call, contradicting REQ-214's own AC3 ('rejected with a :not_registered-shaped :give_up outcome regardless of service_id... :httpc.request/4 is never called'). DEFECT 2 (test-seam gap, also implementation-adjacent): no test seam existed to reach a genuine :advance or genuine retriable outcome -- UrlValidator.validate/1 (called unconditionally inside http_transport/3 at this point in the run) had no injectable resolver and no bypass mechanism, unlike Letflow.Webhooks's own established :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled precedent (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex), so every dispatch attempt against a real local test HTTP server was unconditionally SSRF-blocked before reaching :httpc.request/4 at all -- meaning no test in the suite at this point could prove a genuine 2xx :advance path or a genuine connection-refused/timeout retriable path; every outcome observed was the SSRF-block give-up path. MUTATION-TESTING PASS: ran 6 mutations over the claim/classify/retry logic (claim_due_dispatch_ids/2's :active filter, decide_failure/3's retry-vs-give-up boundary, compute_service_task_backoff_ms/3's call site, the two-step lock's Step-2 id-list filter, handle_success/3's decoded-body pass-through, handle_retry/3's attempt_index increment); found and closed 1 real gap -- config_from_snapshot/1's {:error, _} path was only ever exercised indirectly, behind the SSRF gate, never with a targeted malformed-snapshot test in isolation; added a direct test. Test count in this file grew from an estimated pre-existing ~27 (this backfill cannot recover the exact original count from before this step, since the file has since been reworked further) to 34 at the end of this step. Reported both defects rather than working around them in the test file -- correct role discipline per this project's own TEST-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV boundary.

issues.description: route_kind: :catalog_service never routes to catalog_lookup_stub/2 in do_attempt_dispatch/2 -- every row, regardless of route_kind, is dispatched through http_transport/3's URL path, reaching a real :httpc.request/4 call built from service_id. Contradicts REQ-214's own AC3 (must produce a :not_registered-shaped :give_up outcome, :httpc.request/4 must never be called for this route_kind). Empirically verified via a scratch probe against a synthetic :catalog_service row.

No test seam exists to reach a genuine (non-SSRF-blocked) :advance or genuine retriable outcome -- UrlValidator.validate/1 has no injectable resolver or bypass mechanism, unlike Letflow.Webhooks's own established :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled precedent. Every dispatch attempt in the current test suite is unconditionally SSRF-blocked, so no test proves the real 2xx-success or real-connection-failure code paths actually work end to end.

result.next_action: Route back to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a, rework iteration 2) to fix the :catalog_service routing defect and add a test-only SSRF bypass seam mirroring Letflow.Webhooks's :webhook_ssrf_validation_enabled mechanism, then return to TEST-DESIGNER to add genuine :advance/retriable coverage through the new seam.
